title: Our Favorite GoPro 360 Camera Is Now 40 Percent Off
gist: A WIRED deals piece discounts the GoPro Max 2 360 camera 40% to $299 and notes GoPro still edges out the newer Insta360 X6 on pure video quality despite the X6's greater versatility, while GoPro pushes into the microphone accessory category DJI currently leads.

insights.claim: The GoPro Max 2 remains WIRED's top-pick 360 camera on video-quality grounds even after Insta360 released the newer X6, though the reviewer concedes the X6 is more versatile since it can double as both an action camera and a 360 camera.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.so_what: GoPro retains a quality edge in pure 360 video even as Insta360 out-flanks it on versatility — a narrow but real differentiation GoPro can defend on in a category where Insta360 has been gaining share.
insights.quote: The X6 is more versatile—it can serve double duty as an action camera and 360 camera better than the Max 2—but judged purely on video quality, I prefer the Max 2.
insights.locator: The GoPro Max 2 (7/10 WIRED Recommends) is my favorite 360 camera

insights.claim: At the discounted $299 price, buying a GoPro Max 2 plus a GoPro Hero 13 together costs only about $30 more than a single Insta360 X6, giving GoPro a two-camera bundle price roughly on par with Insta360's one-camera hybrid solution.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.so_what: Illustrates a pricing tactic (stacking discounted SKUs) legacy camera makers can use to blunt price/versatility pressure from newer hybrid entrants like Insta360's X6.
insights.quote: at this price, you can grab the Max 2 and a GoPro Hero 13 for just $30 more than the X6

themes.theme: GoPro's move into audio accessories vs. DJI

insights.claim: The GoPro Max 2's persistent weak point is audio recording quality, and the recommended fix is pairing it with an external Bluetooth microphone rather than relying on the camera's built-in mic.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.so_what: A durable hardware weakness that sustains third-party/accessory attach-rate demand around GoPro's camera line.
insights.quote: e Max 2’s one shortcoming is audio recording quality—it’s not the best. Th
insights.locator: As an action camera, you get all the usual GoPro video modes

insights.claim: GoPro has begun manufacturing its own external microphone, a direct move into the wireless-mic accessory category where DJI's Mic 3 is currently described as the reviewer's favorite external mic.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.so_what: Signals GoPro is expanding vertically into accessory categories to capture spend currently flowing to DJI, worth watching as a new competitive front between the two hardware brands.
insights.quote: GoPro now makes its own microphone, which I am still testing, but DJI’s Mic 3 wireless system is currently our favorite external mic.
insights.locator: GoPro now makes its own microphone

themes.theme: GoPro's flagship closes a legacy weakness

insights.claim: GoPro's current flagship action camera, the Mission 1 Pro, uses a larger 1-inch sensor that the reviewer says has finally fixed low-light performance, historically a persistent weakness across GoPro's action-camera line.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.so_what: Closing a long-standing low-light gap on the flagship model is a meaningful product improvement that could support GoPro's positioning against rivals in the premium action-camera segment.
insights.quote: Low-light performance, once the bane of GoPro cameras, is finally very good in the Mission 1.
insights.locator: The GoPro Mission 1 Pro is the best action camera you can buy
